title: Buttered Corn on the Cob
summary: Husked sweetcorn steamed for 7-10 min until bright yellow and tender, served with butter pats, salt and pepper.

ingredients.item: ears fresh sweetcorn, husks and silk removed
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Husk the corn
steps.text: Pull the husks down from the tip to the stem and rub away the silky threads with your fingers. Snap off any long stems so the ears fit the pot.

steps.title: Steam until tender
steps.text: Bring about 2.5 cm of water to the boil under the steamer basket, lay in the ears, cover and steam on high for 7-10 min. The kernels are ready when they turn bright yellow and burst with sweet juice when pressed; steaming keeps the sugars in the kernels rather than in the water.

steps.title: Butter and serve
steps.text: Lift the corn out with tongs and set a pat of butter on each hot cob to melt. Bring salt and pepper to the table so everyone can season their own.

tips: Buy corn in its husk and cook it the same day; its natural sugars turn to starch quickly after picking.
Do not salt the cooking water heavily or overcook, as the kernels toughen.
Boiling for 4-5 min in a big pot of water works too.
Try flavoured butters with herbs, lime zest or chilli.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Refrigerate leftover cobs wrapped up to 3 days; reheat by steaming 2-3 min until piping hot (74 °C), or cut the kernels off for salads. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
